method: The pasted text is read as characters, never fetched, so the page can only report coordinates that are already written in the link. The shapes are tried in a fixed order and the first match wins: a geo: URI (latitude and longitude, with any ;u= uncertainty or query zoom dropped), a place pin in the data parameters (!3d latitude and !4d longitude), a dropped marker (mlat and mlon, with the map=zoom/lat/lon fragment supplying the zoom), a map view fragment (#map=zoom/latitude/longitude), a centre point (cp=latitude~longitude), a map view centre (@latitude,longitude,zoomz), a named parameter from ll, q, query, center, centre, coordinate, coords, sll, saddr, daddr, destination and origin read as a comma-separated pair, separate lat and lon parameters, and finally a plain decimal pair with optional N, S, E or W letters where S and W make the value negative. Latitude always comes first: a first value between 91 and 180 with a second value inside the latitude range is reported as a probable swap instead of being silently flipped, and every value must stay within -90 to 90 or -180 to 180. Degrees-minutes-seconds is produced by rounding the absolute value to a tenth of an arcsecond and splitting it into whole degrees, minutes and seconds, carrying a rounded 60 seconds into the minute and a rounded 60 minutes into the degree. The decimal places written in the source are kept, trailing zeros included, up to six, and longer values are rounded to six, because the last digit is what states the link's precision: one step is 10 to the power of minus that many places multiplied by 111,320 metres of latitude, and the east-west step is that figure times the cosine of the latitude. A zoom level from 0 to 22 is reported when the link carries one. Short links, address-only links, ISO 6709 strings and reverse geocoding are out of scope, and everything runs in the browser, so nothing is stored, uploaded or sent anywhere.
